stem.text: The functions \( f \), \( g \) and \( h \) are defined by the power series \[ f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n\,x^{n}}{4^{n}}, \qquad g(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 1)^{2n}}{(2n + 1)\,9^{n}}, \qquad h(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(2x - 1)^{n}}{5^{n}} \] for all real \( x \) for which each series converges.

parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the radius of convergence of the series for \( f(x) \).

worked_solution.text: Ratio of consecutive terms in absolute value.
The series converges when |x|/4 < 1, that is |x| < 4.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio (n + 1)x^(n+1)/4^(n+1) divided by n x^n/4^n, or a simplified form such as ((n + 1)/n)(|x|/4), with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of the ratio as |x|/4 with correct limit notation; an error in the limit loses this point.
States the radius of convergence explicitly as 4 (R = 4 or "the radius is 4"); the interval -4 < x < 4 given without naming 4 as the radius does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the radius of convergence of the series for \( g(x) \).

worked_solution.text: Ratio of consecutive terms; the power of x - 1 rises by 2.
The series converges when (x - 1)^2 < 9, that is |x - 1| < 3.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio (x - 1)^(2n+2)/((2n + 3)9^(n+1)) divided by (x - 1)^(2n)/((2n + 1)9^n), or a simplified form such as ((2n + 1)/(2n + 3))((x - 1)^2/9), with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of the ratio as (x - 1)^2/9 (or |x - 1|^2/9) with correct limit notation; an error in the limit loses this point.
States the radius of convergence explicitly as 3, from (x - 1)^2 < 9; giving 9 as the radius, or an interval -2 < x < 4 without naming 3 as the radius, does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Use the ratio test to find the radius of convergence of the series for \( h(x) \).

worked_solution.text: Ratio of consecutive terms in absolute value.
Solve for the distance from the centre 1/2.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio (n + 1)(2x - 1)^(n+1)/5^(n+1) divided by n(2x - 1)^n/5^n, or a simplified form such as ((n + 1)/n)(|2x - 1|/5), with or without absolute values.
Evaluates the limit of the ratio as |2x - 1|/5 (or an equivalent such as 2|x - 1/2|/5) with correct limit notation; an error in the limit loses this point.
States the radius of convergence explicitly as 5/2 (or 2.5), from |x - 1/2| < 5/2; giving 5 as the radius, or an interval -2 < x < 3 without naming 5/2 as the radius, does not earn the point.
